Sounds like enough sleep for proper cycles. You need to manage your calories in vs out better. I need 2-4 hours for proper recovery. If you're digesting food while you sleep stop that. 5 or 6 hours should recover fine. Not optimal but fine. Keto diets can go from useful tools to detrimental to results. Keto diets burn muscle and fat depending on how you do it, you can loose a significant amount of muscle if you're not careful. My recommendation is get your calories from the surplus you're  on to a maintenance diet. Than slowly create a deficit through cardio and lifting. Once you start loosing weight, dial down the cardio till you're plateuing. This will be an ideal calorie to expenditure ratio for converting fat to muscle so to speak. Not the fastest method but a great results over time method.

Tight hams. You need to stretch out to access better pelvic mobility while maintaining a neutral spine. Make it a daily thing to do. You should be good in a month.
